claims: Neil Armstrong became the first person to walk on the Moon on July 20, 1969, during NASA's Apollo 11 mission.
Neil Armstrong is an American astronaut.
Neil Armstrong stepped onto the lunar surface at 10:56 p.m. EDT on July 20, 1969.
Neil Armstrong declared "That's one small step for [a] man, one giant leap for mankind".
Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin explored the lunar surface for over two hours.
Michael Collins orbited above while Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin explored the lunar surface.
Apollo 11 was commanded by Neil Armstrong.
Buzz Aldrin was the Lunar Module Pilot of Apollo 11.
Michael Collins was the Command Module Pilot of Apollo 11.
The Lunar Module Eagle landed at the Sea of Tranquility on July 20, 1969.
The Lunar Module Eagle landed at 4:17 p.m. EDT on July 20, 1969.
The Lunar Module Eagle landed at 20:17 UTC on July 20, 1969.
The Lunar Module Eagle landed with only seconds of fuel remaining.
Neil Armstrong took manual control to avoid a crater during the landing.
Neil Armstrong piloted the craft over hazardous terrain during the landing.
Apollo 11 astronauts spent roughly 212 hours walking on the lunar surface.
Apollo 11 astronauts took photographs on the lunar surface.
Apollo 11 astronauts collected samples on the lunar surface.
Apollo 11 astronauts planted a U.S. flag on the lunar surface.
Apollo 11 team returned safely to Earth on July 24, 1969.
Armstrong and Aldrin’s walk was broadcast to millions.
